intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium
experiences.description: Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, and the famous walk-through shark tunnel. A perfect family activity that avoids the heat and rain, offering an educational and exciting experience for all ages.

experiences.name: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise
experiences.description: Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Enjoy breathtaking Hawaiian sunsets, spot sea turtles and dolphins, and experience the ocean breeze while avoiding peak daytime heat. Many operators include snacks and drinks.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show
experiences.description: Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. This indoor and covered-venue experience showcases the traditions, music, and dance of six Pacific Island cultures, making it ideal for families and perfectly timed to avoid daytime heat.

experiences.name: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking
experiences.description: Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours before temperatures peak. Paddle to the nearby Mokulua Islands, spot sea turtles, and enjoy crystal-clear turquoise waters. Equipment and safety gear are included in the rental.

experiences.name: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits
experiences.description: Visit Hawaii's largest museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Pacific Island cultures. The Science Adventure Center is especially popular with families, offering hands-on volcanic and ocean science activities. A perfect rainy day or high-heat afternoon escape.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Honolulu International Airport at 11:20 AM. Collect luggage, pick up a TheBus pass (affordable public transit), and head to your accommodation. Note: The listed hotel appears to be in Buena Park, CA — for this Hawaii itinerary we assume you are staying at a budget-friendly property near Waikiki such as the Hostelling International Waikiki or a similar budget hotel. Settle in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short walk to Waikiki Beach (free entry). Enjoy your first look at the Pacific Ocean, dip your toes in the warm water, and relax on the sand. Grab a shave ice from a nearby stand (~$4–6) as a welcome treat. Explore the beachfront promenade and get oriented with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Kalakaua Avenue for window shopping and people-watching. Have dinner at a local plate lunch spot such as Rainbow Drive-In, a Honolulu institution offering generous portions of local favorites (loco moco, mixed plate) for under $12. Head back to the hotel early to rest after travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Shave ice and a quick bite from a Waikiki food truck or ABC Store grab-and-go (~$8–10)
meals.dinner: Rainbow Drive-In — plate lunch specials for $10–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the midday arrival and travel fatigue. Purchase a multi-day TheBus pass ($70 for a monthly pass or $3/ride) to save on transportation throughout the trip. August weather averages a high of ~79°F (26°C) with occasional brief showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and head to Diamond Head State Monument (bus-accessible). Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit crater rim for panoramic views of Waikiki and the coastline. Entry fee is $5 per person. Arrive before 8 AM to beat the heat and crowds. Bring water and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, take TheBus to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for snorkeling. Entry is $25 for adults (free for children under 13). Rent snorkel gear on-site (~$12) and explore one of Hawaii's best reef ecosystems. Watch the mandatory marine education video before entering the water. Reservations required — book online in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a sunset walk along the beach. Head to the Duke Kahanamoku Statue for a classic photo. Dinner at Marugame Udon in Waikiki — fresh udon noodles starting at $6, with toppings and tempura available à la carte. Very budget-friendly and family-approved.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit and a pastry from a local grocery store or Foodland (~$5)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the hotel or a convenience store to eat at Hanauma Bay (~$6–8)
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon — $8–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations must be made online at least 2 days in advance. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned at the bay. Bring water shoes for the rocky reef areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus to Kailua on the windward side of Oahu (~1 hour ride, $3). Visit Kailua Beach Park, consistently rated one of the best beaches in the US. The calm, turquoise waters are perfect for families. Enjoy swimming, building sandcastles, and relaxing on the white sand. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or rent bikes (~$15/hour from local shops) along the Kailua beachfront path. Explore the charming Kailua town with its local boutiques and cafes. Visit Lanikai Beach (a short walk or bike ride from Kailua Beach) for more stunning scenery and calm waters ideal for kids.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Honolulu via TheBus. Stop at the Aloha Tower Marketplace at the historic Honolulu Harbor for a waterfront stroll. Enjoy dinner at Panda Express or a local plate lunch counter in the marketplace for a budget-friendly meal. Watch the harbor lights as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua is a local favorite — pancakes and eggs for ~$12–15 (splurge option) OR grab items from a nearby grocery store for ~$6
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — deli sandwiches and local snacks for ~$10–12
meals.dinner: Aloha Tower Marketplace food options — $10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: The windward side of Oahu tends to be greener and slightly rainier due to the trade winds — bring a light rain jacket. Kailua Beach is one of the most family-friendly beaches on the island with lifeguards on duty. The bus ride is scenic and a great way to see the island.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial (free admission to the grounds; USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is free but requires timed-entry passes — reserve online well in advance). This is a deeply moving and historically significant site. The visitor center, museum exhibits, and memorial are all free. Allow 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Pearl Harbor, take TheBus to Aloha Stadium Swap Meet & Marketplace (open Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday — if Tuesday, substitute with a visit to the Bishop Museum instead). Bishop Museum ($24.95 adults, $16.95 children) is Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum with fascinating exhibits on Hawaiian culture, volcanology, and Pacific Island heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a free evening at the beach for sunset. Watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (performances typically Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday evenings at 6:30 PM — check schedule). Grab dinner from a food truck or local eatery.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or grab-and-go from ABC Store (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat at Pearl Harbor picnic areas or grab from the on-site café (~$10–12)
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck (if visiting North Shore area) or local plate lunch near Waikiki — $10–13

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed-entry passes for the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour are FREE but must be reserved online at recreation.gov — they fill up weeks in advance. Arrive early as standby passes are limited. The memorial is closed on Tuesdays, but the visitor center and grounds remain open.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus or join a budget shuttle to the North Shore of Oahu (~1.5 hours). Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park — a stunning beach with calm summer waters (August is the calm season, perfect for swimming). The famous jumping rock is a popular activity for older kids and adults. Entry is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Kam Highway to explore the North Shore surf town of Haleiwa. Browse local art galleries, surf shops, and the famous Matsumoto Shave Ice (~$4–6). Visit Haleiwa Beach Park for more swimming and relaxing. If the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet is open (Wednesday), consider stopping on the way back for affordable local souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Honolulu. Stop at the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (open Wednesday 8 AM–3 PM) for budget souvenir shopping — local crafts, macadamia nuts, and Hawaiian goods at low prices. Return to Waikiki for dinner at a local ramen or poke shop.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before departure from a local bakery or convenience store (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Haleiwa Joe's Haiku Gardens (budget option) or grab a plate lunch from a North Shore food truck — $10–13
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood or a local poke bowl shop in Waikiki — $12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: North Shore waves are calm in summer (May–September), making it safe for family swimming. In winter, waves can reach 30+ feet — not suitable for swimming. The bus journey to North Shore is long but scenic and free with your pass. Bring plenty of sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Honolulu Zoo in Kapiolani Park (adjacent to Waikiki). Admission is $19 for adults and $11 for children (ages 3–12). The zoo features Hawaiian and tropical animals including nene geese (Hawaii's state bird), Galapagos tortoises, and African savanna animals. Great for families with young children. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the zoo, walk across Kapiolani Park to the Waikiki Aquarium ($12 adults, $5 children). One of the oldest aquariums in the US, it features Hawaiian monk seals, colorful reef fish, and coral exhibits. The park itself is free and great for a picnic or frisbee. Enjoy the open green space with Diamond Head as a backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free Kuhio Beach Hula Show (Thursday evenings, check schedule at 6:30 PM). Watch traditional hula performances and live Hawaiian music right on the beach — a wonderful cultural experience at no cost. Grab dinner from a nearby food truck or casual restaurant afterward.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things in Waikiki — famous for pancakes and local breakfast dishes, ~$12–16 per person (popular, arrive early)
meals.lunch: Picnic in Kapiolani Park — pick up supplies from Foodland or Times Supermarket (~$8–10 per person)
meals.dinner: Waikiki food trucks or Musubi Cafe Iyasume — spam musubi and local snacks for $6–10

day_by_day.notes: Kapiolani Park is one of Hawaii's oldest public parks and completely free to enjoy. The combination of the zoo, aquarium, and park makes this a full family day without breaking the budget. Thursday hula shows are a highlight — bring a blanket to sit on the grass.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus to Manoa Falls Trail — a beautiful, easy 1.6-mile round-trip hike through a lush rainforest leading to a 150-foot waterfall. Free to hike (small parking fee if driving, but bus is free with pass). Wear closed-toe shoes as the trail can be muddy. This is a magical experience for families and one of Oahu's most accessible hikes.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, visit the nearby Lyon Arboretum (suggested donation $5) — a stunning 194-acre botanical garden managed by the University of Hawaii. Explore tropical plants, native Hawaiian species, and peaceful garden paths. A great educational experience for kids. Then head to the University of Hawaii Manoa campus for a free self-guided walk.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Chinatown Honolulu for dinner — one of the best areas for affordable, diverse dining. Explore the historic district with its art galleries, lei shops, and local markets. Dine at one of the many affordable Asian restaurants. Friday evenings often feature the Chinatown First Friday art walk (free, family-friendly).

meals.breakfast: Grab items from a local grocery store or hotel before the hike (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks and a light lunch to enjoy after the hike at a park bench (~$6–8)
meals.dinner: Chinatown Honolulu — Little Village Noodle House or Fook Yuen Seafood Restaurant — $10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Manoa Falls trail is best visited in the morning before afternoon rain showers (common in the valley). The trail is muddy — wear shoes you don't mind getting dirty. Bug spray is recommended. The falls are most impressive after recent rainfall. Check trail conditions before going.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the KCC Farmers Market at Kapiolani Community College (open Saturdays 7:30 AM–11 AM, free entry). One of Oahu's best farmers markets with fresh local produce, prepared foods, tropical fruits, and artisan goods. Sample local flavors like fresh pineapple, malasadas, and acai bowls. A wonderful cultural and culinary experience at very low cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park (free) — a large, family-friendly beach park with calm waters, picnic areas, and a beautiful reef-protected lagoon. Great for swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing. Afterward, walk to Ala Moana Center (Hawaii's largest shopping mall) for window shopping and air-conditioned browsing. The mall's food court offers affordable dining options.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset at Ala Moana Beach Park — one of the best sunset viewing spots on Oahu. Then head to the nearby Ward Village area for dinner. Visit Dave's Ice Cream for a classic Hawaiian dessert (~$4–6) to end the evening. Saturday nights often feature live music at various venues along Waikiki.

meals.breakfast: KCC Farmers Market — fresh local breakfast items, acai bowls, malasadas for $8–12
meals.lunch: Ala Moana Center food court — wide variety of options from $8–13 per person
meals.dinner: Nico's Pier 38 near the harbor — fresh fish and local plates for $12–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: The KCC Farmers Market is a must-do Saturday activity — arrive early as popular vendors sell out quickly. Ala Moana Beach Park has lifeguards and restroom facilities. The beach is popular with local families on weekends, giving you an authentic glimpse of local Hawaiian life.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Polynesian Cultural Center on the windward coast (~1 hour by bus). Note: Full admission is $59.95–$119.95 per person, which may be a splurge for budget travelers. Budget alternative: Visit the Laie Hawaii Temple grounds (free, beautiful gardens) nearby, and spend the morning at Malaekahana Beach State Recreation Area (free) — a stunning, uncrowded beach with calm waters and a small island (Goat Island) accessible by wading at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Malaekahana Beach and wade out to Mokuauia (Goat Island) — a small seabird sanctuary with pristine beaches. This is a unique, free adventure that feels like a private island experience. Bring snorkel gear if you have it for excellent reef snorkeling around the island. Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu via TheBus. Stop at the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet if open for any last-minute souvenir shopping. Enjoy a relaxed dinner back in Waikiki. Consider trying a Hawaiian plate lunch from Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award-winning local institution) — authentic Hawaiian food at reasonable prices.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from the hotel or grab items from a convenience store before departure (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch to enjoy at Malaekahana Beach (~$8–10 per person from a grocery store)
meals.dinner: Helena's Hawaiian Food — authentic kalua pig, laulau, and poi for $12–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Mokuauia (Goat Island) is accessible only at low tide — check tide charts before visiting. The crossing is about waist-deep and 200 yards. Do not attempt in rough surf. The island is a protected seabird sanctuary — stay on the beach and do not disturb nesting birds. This is one of Oahu's hidden gems.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning back at Waikiki Beach for one last swim and relaxation session. Collect any last shells or photos. Visit the Moana Surfrider Hotel's historic banyan tree courtyard (free to walk through) — the hotel dates to 1901 and is a beautiful piece of Hawaiian history. Grab a final shave ice from your favorite stand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the International Market Place in Waikiki or the ABC Stores (affordable local gifts, macadamia nuts, Kona coffee). Pack your bags and check out of the hotel. Head to Honolulu International Airport via TheBus (Route 20 from Waikiki, ~45 minutes, $3). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before your departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Honolulu. Reflect on 10 wonderful days in Hawaii — from stunning beaches and lush rainforest hikes to rich cultural experiences and delicious local food, all on a budget. Mahalo and safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a local spot — Liliha Bakery for coco puffs and breakfast plates (~$10–14) or grab-and-go from a convenience store (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the International Market Place food hall or a quick bite before heading to the airport (~$10–13)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal — budget $12–18 for airport food

day_by_day.notes: TheBus Route 20 (Airport Express) runs from Waikiki to the airport and is the most budget-friendly transfer option at $3. Allow extra time as traffic can be heavy on Monday afternoons. Ensure all checked bags meet airline weight limits — Hawaiian souvenirs can add up! Confirm your return flight details the night before.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

The Science Adventure Center is especially popular with families, offering hands-on volcanic and ocean science activities. A perfect rainy day or high-heat afternoon escape.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer to hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll around the local Buena Park area to get oriented. Visit a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first dinner close to the hotel to recover from travel. Explore the Orangethorpe Ave dining strip for a casual family-friendly meal.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Quick casual bite near the hotel — try a local deli or fast-casual spot on Orangethorpe Ave
meals.dinner: BJ's Restaurant & Brewhouse nearby — family-friendly with a broad mid-range menu including pizzas, burgers, and salads (~$15–$25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Prioritize rest so the family is energized for the full days ahead. Confirm all activity bookings and check weather forecasts for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits — Hawaii's largest museum with world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Polynesian culture. Perfect for families and a great introduction to Hawaiian heritage. Opens at 9:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for the first beach experience of the trip. Rent beach chairs and umbrellas, splash in the calm surf, and let the kids build sandcastles. The beach is walkable from many Waikiki hotels and has lifeguards on duty.
day_by_day.evening: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise — set sail on a family-friendly catamaran along Waikiki Beach during the cooler evening hours. Watch the stunning Hawaiian sunset over the Pacific Ocean. Book in advance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try Liliha Bakery for famous coco puffs and local pastries
meals.lunch: Grab plate lunches near the Bishop Museum — Rainbow Drive-In is a beloved local institution with affordable Hawaiian plate lunches (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant with Hawaiian-inspired seafood and burgers, mid-range pricing (~$20–$35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is indoors and air-conditioned — ideal if morning rain occurs (176mm average rainfall this month). Book the catamaran cruise ahead of time as sunset slots fill quickly in August.

day_by_day.morning: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking — enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours. Kailua is one of Hawaii's most beautiful beaches with turquoise water and gentle conditions perfect for kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, relax on Kailua Beach — one of the finest beaches in all of Hawaii. Explore the charming Kailua town for boutique shopping, local art galleries, and shave ice stands. Walk the beachfront path.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Waikiki/Honolulu area. Enjoy a relaxed family dinner and early evening to rest after an active day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before kayaking — Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua is a local favorite for pancakes and eggs (~$12–$18 per person)
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua — beloved local deli with fresh sandwiches, salads, and local snacks (~$10–$15)
meals.dinner: Buzz's Original Steakhouse in Kailua — casual, family-friendly steakhouse with great local atmosphere (~$25–$40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is about 30–40 minutes from Waikiki by car. Start the kayaking tour early (8:00–9:00 AM) to beat the heat and afternoon winds. Apply reef-safe sunscreen — it's required in Hawaii.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore of Oahu — visit Waimea Bay Beach Park for a scenic morning walk and beach time. In August, the summer swells are calm making it safe for swimming. Stop at the famous Waimea Valley for a short nature walk to the waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the North Shore — visit Haleiwa town for shave ice at Matsumoto's (a Hawaii institution), browse surf shops, and enjoy the laid-back surf culture. Stop at Sunset Beach for photos and a beach walk.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Honolulu. Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show — experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' luau and cultural show. This is a highlight of any Hawaii family trip with fire dancing, music, and Polynesian storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast on the road — Sunrise Shack on the North Shore for açaí bowls and smoothies (~$10–$14)
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — legendary garlic shrimp plates, a North Shore must-do (~$14–$16)
meals.dinner: Included luau dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — buffet-style Hawaiian feast included with the evening show ticket

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is in Laie on the North Shore, making it a logical end to a North Shore day. Book 'Ha: Breath of Life' tickets well in advance — it sells out frequently. The show typically starts at 7:30 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument — hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit crater for panoramic views of Waikiki and Honolulu. The hike takes about 1.5–2 hours and is suitable for older children. Start early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for snorkeling — one of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots with abundant marine life in a protected bay. Reserve entry online in advance (required). Gear rentals available on-site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a leisurely evening stroll along Kalakaua Avenue. Browse the International Market Place for souvenirs and gifts. Enjoy a beachside dinner as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the Diamond Head hike — Bogart's Café near Diamond Head for açaí bowls and coffee (~$10–$15)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or grab food near Hanauma Bay — Kona Brewing Company in Hawaii Kai is a short drive away with great burgers and craft drinks (~$18–$28)
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon in Waikiki — incredibly popular, affordable, and delicious Japanese udon noodles, perfect for families (~$8–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — book as soon as possible as slots fill up weeks ahead. Diamond Head trail opens at 6:00 AM; arriving early avoids crowds and heat. Bring water and snacks for both activities.

day_by_day.morning: Fly to Maui (short inter-island flight, approximately 30–40 minutes). Settle into Maui accommodations and pick up a rental car. Head to Ka'anapali Beach — one of Maui's most beautiful resort beaches with calm, clear water ideal for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Maui Ocean Center Aquarium in Ma'alaea — Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, sharks, and coral reef ecosystems. Excellent for all ages and a great indoor option if afternoon showers occur.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming town of Lahaina — stroll Front Street, browse art galleries, and watch the sunset from the historic waterfront. The famous Banyan Tree Park is a must-see.

meals.breakfast: Airport breakfast or hotel — grab a quick bite before the flight
meals.lunch: Café O'Lei at the Maui Ocean Center — convenient, fresh, and family-friendly with ocean views (~$14–$22)
meals.dinner: Lahaina Fish Co. on Front Street — fresh local seafood with an open-air waterfront setting, mid-range pricing (~$22–$38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest well in advance. Maui accommodations should be pre-booked — consider a condo or suite for family comfort. The Maui Ocean Center is best visited in the afternoon when beach heat peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Road to Hana — one of the world's most scenic coastal drives. Stop at Twin Falls for a short waterfall hike, Wai'anapanapa State Park for the famous black sand beach, and various scenic lookouts along the way. Start early.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana experience — visit the Garden of Eden Arboretum for lush tropical gardens, or stop at Ke'anae Peninsula for dramatic coastal views. Enjoy a picnic lunch at one of the scenic pullouts.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Hana (the drive back takes 2–2.5 hours). Arrive back at your Maui base for a relaxed dinner. Rest early after a long but spectacular day.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from a local grocery store the night before — eat in the car or at Twin Falls
meals.lunch: Roadside food stands along the Road to Hana — try fresh banana bread from Aunty Sandy's in Ke'anae (~$5–$8) and local fruit stands
meals.dinner: Paia Fish Market in Paia town on the way back — casual, beloved local spot with fresh fish tacos and plates (~$14–$22)

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day commitment — start no later than 7:30 AM. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations. The road has 620 curves and 59 bridges — take it slow and enjoy the journey. Not recommended for those prone to car sickness.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive to Haleakala National Park summit (10,023 ft elevation) to witness the sunrise above the clouds — a truly magical and unforgettable experience. Dress in warm layers as summit temperatures can be near 10°C even in August. Reserve a sunrise permit in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakala and warm up. Head to Wailea Beach — one of Maui's most beautiful resort beaches with calm, crystal-clear water. Relax, swim, and enjoy the afternoon sunshine. Explore the Wailea Beach Walk.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special family dinner in Wailea or Kihei to celebrate a memorable day. Watch the sunset from the beach before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack warm snacks and hot drinks in a thermos for the Haleakala summit — it's too cold and remote for a sit-down breakfast up top
meals.lunch: Kihei Caffe in Kihei — beloved local breakfast/lunch spot open all day with generous portions (~$12–$18)
meals.dinner: Monkeypod Kitchen in Wailea — farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine with great cocktails and a lively family atmosphere (~$22–$38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise permits must be reserved at recreation.gov — they open 60 days in advance and sell out immediately. Set an alarm: you'll need to leave your hotel by 3:00–4:00 AM to reach the summit in time. Bring jackets, gloves, and blankets for the whole family.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkeling at Molokini Crater — a partially submerged volcanic crater offshore with exceptional visibility and abundant marine life. Join a guided boat snorkel tour departing from Ma'alaea Harbor. Tours typically depart at 7:00–8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Molokini by midday. Spend the afternoon at Makena Beach (Big Beach) — one of Maui's largest and most dramatic beaches. Relax, bodysurf the gentle shore break, and soak in the stunning scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Maui — return to Lahaina or your resort area for a farewell Maui dinner. Browse for last-minute souvenirs and enjoy the warm tropical evening.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the boat tour — most tour operators provide light snacks on board
meals.lunch: Post-snorkel lunch at Makena Landing area — South Maui Fish Co. food truck for fresh poke bowls (~$14–$18)
meals.dinner: Merriman's Maui in Kapalua — upscale-casual farm-to-ocean dining with stunning sunset views, a special farewell meal (~$35–$55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Molokini snorkel tour in advance — Trilogy Excursions and Pride of Maui are reputable family-friendly operators. Molokini tours often include breakfast and lunch on board. Makena Beach has no lifeguards — supervise children carefully near the water.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last beach walk. Pack up and check out of Maui accommodations. If time allows, stop at a local farmers market or pick up fresh Hawaiian coffee, macadamia nuts, and local jams as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Maui's Kahului Airport for the inter-island flight back to Honolulu (if connecting) or direct mainland flight. Allow extra time for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaii adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Travel home — in-flight meal or airport dining. Arrive home with wonderful memories, a healthy tan, and a suitcase full of Hawaiian souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Final Hawaiian breakfast — Da Kitchen in Kahului for generous local-style breakfast plates (~$12–$18)
meals.lunch: Airport dining at Kahului Airport — local options available in the terminal
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or dining at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Kahului Airport at least 2 hours before departure (2.5 hours recommended for mainland flights). Ensure all checked bags meet airline weight limits — Hawaiian souvenirs add up! Double-check that no restricted agricultural items (fresh fruits, plants, soil) are packed in luggage heading to the mainland.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium
experiences.description: Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, and the famous walk-through shark tunnel. A perfect family activity that avoids the heat and rain, offering an educational and exciting experience for all ages.

experiences.name: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise
experiences.description: Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Enjoy breathtaking Hawaiian sunsets, spot sea turtles and dolphins, and experience the ocean breeze while avoiding peak daytime heat. Many operators include snacks and drinks.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show
experiences.description: Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. This indoor and covered-venue experience showcases the traditions, music, and dance of six Pacific Island cultures, making it ideal for families and perfectly timed to avoid daytime heat.

experiences.name: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking
experiences.description: Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours before temperatures peak. Paddle to the nearby Mokulua Islands, spot sea turtles, and enjoy crystal-clear turquoise waters. Equipment and safety gear are included in the rental.

experiences.name: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits
experiences.description: Visit Hawaii's largest museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Pacific Island cultures. The Science Adventure Center is especially popular with families, offering hands-on volcanic and ocean science activities. A perfect rainy day or high-heat afternoon escape.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii — Flight Alaska lands at 11:20 AM. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from the airport to your luxury accommodation and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your hotel and settle in. Take a leisurely stroll along the nearest beach to acclimate to the island atmosphere. Enjoy the warm Hawaiian sun and turquoise waters at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Waikiki Beach Evening Sunset Catamaran Cruise — Set sail on a family-friendly catamaran cruise during the cooler evening hours along Waikiki Beach. Watch the stunning Hawaiian sunset over the Pacific Ocean while enjoying light refreshments on board.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — iconic beachfront restaurant offering fresh Hawaiian seafood and island-inspired cuisine with stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion dining experience with premium sushi and signature black cod dishes

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule light to allow for jet lag recovery and settling in. Confirm catamaran cruise booking in advance as sunset slots fill up quickly in August.

day_by_day.morning: Kailua Beach Morning Family Kayaking — Enjoy a guided family kayaking adventure at the calm and sheltered Kailua Beach during the cooler morning hours. Paddle through crystal-clear waters and explore the scenic coastline, with expert guides ensuring a safe and memorable experience for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Kailua Beach — one of Hawaii's most pristine white-sand beaches. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas, snorkel in the calm turquoise waters, and enjoy the natural beauty of the windward coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki area for a relaxed evening. Explore the upscale shops at Royal Hawaiian Center and enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant at the Ilima Hotel — famous for their fluffy pancakes and local Hawaiian breakfast favorites
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Café & Deli in Kailua — beloved local spot with gourmet sandwiches, fresh salads, and artisan coffee
meals.dinner: The Pig and the Lady — award-winning Honolulu restaurant blending Vietnamese and Hawaiian flavors with locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach is approximately 30–40 minutes from central Honolulu. Book kayaking tour in advance. August mornings are ideal for kayaking before afternoon trade winds pick up.

day_by_day.morning: Bishop Museum Interactive Science and Culture Exhibits — Visit Hawaii's largest and most prestigious museum featuring world-class indoor exhibits on Hawaiian history, natural science, and Polynesian culture. Explore the iconic Hawaiian Hall, planetarium shows, and hands-on science exhibits perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic Iolani Palace — the only royal palace on American soil — for a guided tour. Explore the beautifully restored rooms and learn about Hawaii's royal history. Afterward, stroll through the Capitol District and browse the Honolulu Farmers Market.
day_by_day.evening: Polynesian Cultural Center Evening Show — Experience the award-winning 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening luau and cultural show at the Polynesian Cultural Center. Enjoy a premium luau dinner followed by a breathtaking theatrical performance celebrating Polynesian heritage.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things — iconic Honolulu breakfast spot famous for their crepes, waffles, and fresh tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Livestock Tavern — Honolulu's celebrated farm-to-table restaurant with artisan burgers and locally sourced seasonal dishes
meals.dinner: Included in the Polynesian Cultural Center luau package — a lavish buffet featuring traditional Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is located on the North Shore (approximately 1 hour from Honolulu). Book the Ambassador VIP package for the best experience including reserved front-row seating and private dining. The evening show typically runs until 9:30 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Fly to Maui — Take an early inter-island flight (approximately 30 minutes). Check in to your luxury Maui resort. Freshen up and head to Ka'anapali Beach, consistently ranked among the world's best beaches, for a morning swim and snorkel session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Maui Ocean Center Aquarium — Explore Hawaii's premier aquarium featuring stunning indoor exhibits of tropical fish, sea turtles, sharks, and vibrant coral reef ecosystems. The open-ocean tunnel and touch pools are especially engaging for families. Spend 2–3 hours exploring all exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Ka'anapali Beach — Watch the legendary Cliff Diver ceremony at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) as a local diver leaps from the lava rock at sunset, a nightly Maui tradition. Enjoy cocktails at a beachfront bar.

meals.breakfast: In-room dining at your Honolulu hotel before departure — fresh tropical fruit, pastries, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman in Ka'anapali — farm-to-table Maui cuisine with handcrafted cocktails and stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Lahaina Grill — Maui's most celebrated fine dining restaurant with innovative American cuisine and an award-winning wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines for the most reliable service. Confirm Maui luxury resort reservation (recommend Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea or Montage Kapalua Bay). Maui Ocean Center is best visited in the afternoon to avoid morning crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana Sunrise Drive — Embark on the iconic Road to Hana, one of the world's most scenic coastal drives. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, explore the Garden of Eden Arboretum, and marvel at the dramatic sea cliffs and lush rainforest scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana — Visit the black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park, explore the sacred Pools of 'Ohe'o (Seven Sacred Pools) in Haleakalā National Park, and hike the short Pipiwai Trail through a bamboo forest to Waimoku Falls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Maui resort. Unwind with a luxury spa treatment at the resort spa — choose from traditional Hawaiian lomilomi massage or a couple's oceanfront treatment.

meals.breakfast: Café des Amis in Paia — charming French-Moroccan café with fresh crepes, smoothie bowls, and organic coffee before the drive
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by your resort or picked up from Paia's gourmet deli — enjoy at a scenic roadside stop along the Hana Highway
meals.dinner: Mama's Fish House — Maui's most iconic and beloved restaurant, featuring ultra-fresh fish caught daily by local fishermen, with a romantic oceanfront setting

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day commitment (approximately 10–12 hours round trip). Start early (by 7:00 AM) to beat traffic and maximize daylight. Consider hiring a private driver or guided tour for a more relaxed experience. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakalā Sunrise Experience — Wake before dawn for the spectacular sunrise above the clouds at Haleakalā Crater (summit elevation 10,023 ft). Watch the sky transform in breathtaking colors as the sun rises over the volcanic crater. Bring warm layers as temperatures near the summit can drop to 5–10°C.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to sea level and visit Upcountry Maui — explore the charming town of Makawao, browse local art galleries, and visit the Ali'i Kula Lavender Farm for a guided tour through fragrant lavender fields with panoramic island views.
day_by_day.evening: Wailea Beach sunset stroll — Walk along the Wailea Beach Path, a 1.5-mile coastal promenade connecting Maui's most luxurious resort beaches. Enjoy the golden hour light and warm evening breeze.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise snacks and hot beverages at the Haleakalā Visitor Center — pack thermos coffee and pastries from your resort the night before
meals.lunch: Hali'imaile General Store — legendary Upcountry Maui restaurant by Chef Bev Gannon, serving innovative Hawaiian Regional Cuisine in a historic pineapple plantation building
meals.dinner: Spago Maui at Four Seasons Wailea — Wolfgang Puck's acclaimed restaurant featuring California-Hawaiian fusion cuisine with stunning ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā Sunrise requires a timed entry reservation through the National Park Service (recreation.gov) — book well in advance as slots sell out months ahead. Depart resort by 3:00–3:30 AM for the summit. The drive takes approximately 1.5 hours from Wailea.

day_by_day.morning: Molokini Crater Snorkeling Expedition — Board a premium catamaran for a morning snorkeling trip to Molokini Crater, a partially submerged volcanic caldera teeming with over 250 species of tropical fish and crystal-clear visibility up to 150 feet. Premium tours include snorkel gear, wetsuits, and continental breakfast on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wailea Beach Afternoon — Return to your resort and spend a relaxing afternoon at Wailea Beach. Enjoy premium beach service, paddleboarding, or a private surfing lesson with a certified instructor.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Maui Luau — Attend the Grand Wailea's or Andaz Maui's premium luau experience featuring traditional Hawaiian food, live music, hula performances, and fire knife dancing under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast included on the Molokini snorkeling catamaran
meals.lunch: Ferraro's Bar e Ristorante at Four Seasons Maui — elegant Italian-Mediterranean cuisine served steps from the ocean with breathtaking views
meals.dinner: Luau dinner included in the evening luau package — traditional kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Book the Molokini snorkeling trip with Pride of Maui or Trilogy Excursions for the best premium experience. Morning departures (7:00–7:30 AM) offer the calmest sea conditions and best visibility. Confirm luau reservation at least 2 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Fly to the Big Island (Hawaii Island) — Take an early inter-island flight to Kona or Hilo. Check in to your luxury Big Island resort. Visit Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area — one of Hawaii's largest and most beautiful white-sand beaches — for a morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — Explore one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Walk the Kilauea Iki Trail through a hardened lava lake, visit the Thurston Lava Tube, and view the glowing Halema'uma'u Crater from the Jaggar Museum overlook.
day_by_day.evening: Lava viewing at dusk — If conditions permit, join a guided evening lava tour to witness the dramatic glow of active lava flows against the darkening sky — one of Hawaii's most unforgettable natural spectacles.

meals.breakfast: Brown's Beach House at Fairmont Orchid — elegant oceanfront breakfast with fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Café Pesto in Hilo — beloved local restaurant with wood-fired pizzas, fresh seafood, and creative island-inspired dishes
meals.dinner: Merriman's Waimea — Peter Merriman's flagship farm-to-table restaurant, the birthplace of Hawaii Regional Cuisine, featuring locally sourced beef, fish, and produce

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park is approximately 45 minutes from Hilo and 2.5 hours from Kona. Check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current volcanic activity updates. Evening lava tours require advance booking with a licensed guide.

day_by_day.morning: Manta Ray Night Snorkeling Preparation and Morning Relaxation — Spend a leisurely morning at your resort pool or beach. Enjoy a late breakfast and prepare for the day's adventures. Optional: visit the historic Pu'uhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park (Place of Refuge) for a guided cultural tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kohala Coast Exploration — Drive the scenic Kohala Coast and visit the ancient Pu'ukohola Heiau National Historic Site. Explore the charming town of Hawi and browse local art galleries and boutiques. Stop at Pololu Valley Lookout for dramatic panoramic views of the rugged northern coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Manta Ray Night Snorkeling — Experience one of Hawaii's most magical wildlife encounters: snorkeling with giant Pacific manta rays (wingspan up to 14 feet) as they feed on plankton illuminated by underwater lights off the Kona Coast. A truly unforgettable family experience.

meals.breakfast: Daylight Mind Coffee Company in Kailua-Kona — artisan coffee roaster with farm-to-table breakfast bowls and stunning ocean views
meals.lunch: Bamboo Restaurant in Hawi — charming plantation-era building serving creative Pacific Rim cuisine with local ingredients
meals.dinner: Huggo's on the Rocks in Kailua-Kona — romantic open-air restaurant perched over the ocean, serving fresh local fish and premium steaks with spectacular sunset views

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray snorkeling tours depart from Keauhou Bay or Garden Eel Cove in the evening (typically 5:30–8:30 PM). Book with Manta Ray Advocates or Jack's Diving Locker for a responsible, eco-certified experience. Manta ray sightings are not guaranteed but occur on approximately 85–90% of tours.

day_by_day.morning: Waipio Valley Horseback Ride or ATV Tour — Descend into the dramatic Waipio Valley, the 'Valley of the Kings,' for a guided horseback ride or ATV adventure through taro fields, past waterfalls, and along a stunning black sand beach. This sacred valley was once home to Hawaiian royalty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Honolulu — Take an afternoon inter-island flight back to Oahu. Spend your final afternoon shopping for premium Hawaiian gifts and souvenirs at Ala Moana Center (the largest open-air shopping mall in the world) or the luxury boutiques at Royal Hawaiian Center.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Honolulu — Celebrate your final evening in Hawaii with a world-class dining experience. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar before your farewell dinner, reflecting on 10 unforgettable days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Café Pesto or resort in-room dining — fresh tropical fruit, macadamia nut pancakes, and Kona coffee for a final Big Island breakfast
meals.lunch: MW Restaurant in Honolulu — Chef Wade Ueoka's acclaimed restaurant celebrating Hawaii's multicultural culinary heritage with refined local ingredients
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani Hotel — Honolulu's most prestigious fine dining restaurant, offering classic French cuisine with Hawaiian influences in an elegant oceanfront setting; Zagat-rated and AAA Five Diamond awarded

day_by_day.notes: Waipio Valley requires a 4WD vehicle to descend the steep 25% grade road — guided tours are the safest and most informative option. Confirm return flight to Honolulu and onward departure logistics. La Mer requires formal attire (collared shirts for men) and advance reservations. Allow extra time for airport check-in on departure day.
